question: What is the primary goal of permanent methods of contraception?

options.A: To regulate irregular menstrual cycles and reduce heavy bleeding
options.B: To offer a permanent end to childbearing for those with complete families
options.C: To protect the reproductive tract against sexually transmitted infections
options.D: To provide a temporary break in childbearing for young mothers

explanation: Permanent methods are designed specifically for clients who are completely sure they do not want any more children in the future. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T5#BMP126_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why should midwives emphasize the permanent nature of sterilization during client talks?

options.A: Surgical reversals are simple procedures easily done at primary health centers
options.B: Reversal operations are costly, complicated, and have a low success rate
options.C: The body naturally restores fertility within two years after the surgery
options.D: Hormonal injections can easily override the surgical blockage later

explanation: Because reversing a sterilization surgery is difficult and rarely restores full fertility, clients must view the decision as absolute and irreversible. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T5#BMP126_U2_T5_h1)

question: What important protection do permanent methods fail to provide to the client?

options.A: Protection against unwanted and unplanned pregnancies
options.B: Protection against heavy monthly menstrual bleeding
options.D: Protection against normal age-related hormonal changes

explanation: Surgical sterilization only blocks the passage of eggs or sperm, meaning barrier methods like condoms are still required for STI protection. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T5#BMP126_U2_T5_h2)

question: A client requests a tubal ligation because her husband is forcing her to do it. What is your best action as the midwife?

options.A: Book the surgery immediately to satisfy the demands of the spouse
options.B: Provide private counseling to ensure the decision is truly voluntary by the client
options.C: Perform the procedure quietly without documenting the husband's involvement
options.D: Refuse service entirely and report the couple to local community leaders

explanation: Informed consent requires that the choice is entirely voluntary and free from coercion by anyone, including a spouse. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T5#BMP126_U2_T5_h2)

question: Which anatomical structure is blocked or cut during female sterilization surgery?
explanation: Tubal ligation physically blocks the fallopian tubes so that sperm cannot travel upward to fertilize an egg released from the ovary. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T5#BMP126_U2_T5_h3)

question: Why is a minilaparotomy often performed shortly after a woman gives birth?

options.A: Hormonal changes make the fallopian tubes completely insensitive to pain
options.B: The abdominal wall has no nerves at that time, requiring no local anesthesia
options.C: The uterus is still enlarged and brings the fallopian tubes close to the incision
options.D: Postpartum mothers heal completely within twenty-four hours of delivery

explanation: Immediately after delivery, the high position of the fundus makes accessing the fallopian tubes through a small abdominal cut much easier. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T5#BMP126_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which tube is cut and tied during a male vasectomy procedure?
explanation: The vas deferens is the muscular tube that transports sperm from the testes, and sealing it prevents sperm from mixing with semen. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T5#BMP126_U2_T5_h4)

question: Why must a man continue using a backup contraceptive method immediately after a vasectomy?

options.A: Sperm already stored in the tubes above the surgical site can still cause pregnancy for a while
options.B: Hormonal levels in the male body remain unchanged until cleared by special drugs
options.C: The surgery takes several weeks to stop the testicles from producing new sperm cells
options.D: The stitches in the scrotum dissolve too quickly to maintain a proper physical seal

explanation: Stored sperm remain in the reproductive tract above the blockage and must be cleared out through repeated ejaculations before the man is fully sterile. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T5#BMP126_U2_T5_h4)

question: What is NOT a recommended instruction for a client recovering from a sterilization procedure?

options.A: Engage in heavy farm work and rigorous exercise immediately
options.B: Return to the clinic for a follow-up visit after one week
options.C: Keep the surgical wound clean and dry for at least two days
options.D: Take simple pain relievers like paracetamol for mild discomfort

explanation: Strenuous physical activity should be avoided during the first week to allow the surgical incision to heal properly. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T5#BMP126_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why do clients often need reassurance that sterilization will not affect their sexual drive?

options.A: Permanent contraception stops the body from producing natural sweat and body oils
options.B: Men and women experience immediate weight gain after the surgical procedure
options.C: The surgery alters nerve pathways that control sexual feelings in the pelvic region
options.D: Many people confuse sterilization with the removal of hormone-producing sex glands

explanation: Clients often worry that tying tubes or cutting the vas deferens will ruin their sex life, but sexual organs and hormones remain completely unaffected. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T5#BMP126_U2_T5_h5)

question: Which widespread community myth about vasectomy causes the most unnecessary fear among men?

options.A: It permanently increases physical body weight within days
options.B: It causes men to grow facial hair much faster than normal
options.C: It automatically cures chronic high blood pressure and diabetes
options.D: It is the exact same medical procedure as full castration

explanation: Many men fear vasectomy because they mistakenly believe it involves removing the testicles, whereas only the tiny tubes carrying sperm are blocked. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T5#BMP126_U2_T5_h6)

question: How should a midwife respond to a community member who believes female sterilization causes mental illness?

options.A: Suggest that only older women with stable mental health should undergo the procedure
options.B: Advise the woman to take herbal medications to protect her brain after surgery
options.C: Agree with the rumor because abdominal surgeries can disturb brain chemicals
options.D: Explain that reproductive organs are separate from the brain and hormones remain normal

explanation: Educating clients patiently with basic anatomy helps dispel false fears linking reproductive surgery to mental health problems. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T5#BMP126_U2_T5_h6)
